question.problem: Consider the equivalence relation $∼$ on the set $A={0,1,2,…,20},$ defined by $a∼b$ if $5∣(b-a).$   How many distinct equivalence classes does $∼$ partition $A$ into?
question.worked_solution:
The equivalence classes of $∼$ partition $A,$ meaning that any element $a\in A$ belongs to exactly one distinct equivalence class.

So, we compute equivalence classes until all the elements of $A$ have been placed into an equivalence class.

$$
\begin{aligned}[0] & ={a\in A\,:\,a∼0} \\  & ={a\in A\,:\,5∣(a-0)} \\  & ={a\in A\,:\,5∣a} \\  & ={0,5,10,15,20} \\  \\ [1] & ={a\in A\,:\,a∼1} \\  & ={a\in A\,:\,5∣(a-1)} \\  & ={1,6,11,16} \\  \\ [2] & ={a\in A\,:\,a∼2} \\  & ={a\in A\,:\,5∣(a-2)} \\  & ={2,7,12,17} \\  \\ [3] & ={a\in A\,:\,a∼3} \\  & ={a\in A\,:\,5∣(a-3)} \\  & ={3,8,13,18} \\  \\ [4] & ={a\in A\,:\,a∼4} \\  & ={a\in A\,:\,5∣(a-4)} \\  & ={4,9,14,19} \\ \end{aligned}
$$

All of the elements of $A$ have been placed into an equivalence class, so we are done.

We have $5$ distinct equivalence classes:

$$
[0]={0,5,10,15,20},\,[1]={1,6,11,16},\,[2]={2,7,12,17},\,[3]={3,8,13,18},\,[4]={4,9,14,19}.
$$

Notice that the equivalence classes form a partition of $A,$ as expected.
